function.name: place
function.description:
Put an item from the counter into the machine and let physics settle it. Counts one action when accepted; a refused call changes nothing and costs nothing.
What happens: (1) the pose is rounded to 1 mm and 1 degree; (2) it is refused if the item would overlap anything there by more than 0.5 mm (collision_at_pose: penetration_mm and colliding_with say how deep and with what); (3) it is refused if the item cannot reach the pose by a straight path from above the basket, or along insert_dir for mode insert (not_insertable, blocked_by), or if the basket is pushed in (not_insertable, blocked_by tub: pull it out with set_rack first), or if the pose is outside the frame (out_of_bounds); (4) the item is lowered straight down until it touches something and let go at rest, so give a position a little above where it should end; (5) it settles under gravity and friction; (6) it is nudged lightly from four sides to see whether it stays. Mode insert pushes the item along insert_dir with the force of a hand and can nudge neighbours aside on the way, but the end pose itself must still be free of the machine: it cannot press an item down between tines that are closer together than it is thick.
The result of the drop: released_at (where the item was let go), displacement_mm and rotation_deg (how far it went from there until it lay still), settle_time_s, stable, resting, contact_forces_N (what it touches, each with the force on it in newtons), and only when they apply fell_through (it went through the basket), fell_out (it left the basket) and returned (items that ended on the kitchen floor and are back on the counter).
What every accepted action returns after that. changes is everything the action changed in the scene, completely: changes.items holds the whole new entry (item_id, the frame its pose is in, position_mm, quat_wxyz, stable, touches, location) of every item whose entry is new or different, among them the item just placed with the pose it came to rest in, and for an item displaced by more than 1 mm or 1 degree also moved_mm and turned_deg; changes.to_counter names the items that left the machine; changes.racks, changes.rack_options and changes.phase say what else changed. An item that is not named in changes is exactly where and how it was. The scene is not repeated: keep track of it from the changes, or ask get_state (one query) for the whole of it or a part. load is the whole load in a few numbers (items placed and on the counter, placed items by_location, the ids of those that are unstable, where each basket is), budget the counters as used/allowed, state_hash the start of the hash of the scene. An action carries the whole scene as state (as get_state gives it) in place of changes only when this client has not yet been given the whole scene: no get_state without rack or items, and no accepted action before it.
Reading it. displacement_mm and rotation_deg say how far the item went after it was let go, not whether that was good: a plate dropped from a suggested place above the tines falls 60 to 80 mm to the base and leans over 10 to 20 degrees, which is a correct drop, while a bowl that moved 6 mm may be perched on the tine tips. resting says which: lowest_point_mm is the height of its lowest point above the top of the base grid, on_base is true within 10 mm of it (the item stands on the floor of the basket) and false when it is held up by tines, a shelf or other items; force_over_weight is the sum of its contact forces over its weight, about 1 for an item that simply rests and several for one wedged between things (a plate jammed against the cutlery basket). rotation_deg is the angle of the whole turn, about whatever axis: 45 degrees or more most often means the item tipped over, but a piece of cutlery let down into a cell often turns by about 90 about its own length and still stands there, and reads the same; resting, touches and a picture say which. stable is the light nudge of step 6, and false as well for an item the nudge left standing that only balances (it touches nothing sideways and stands on a base so narrow that a tilt of 5 degrees would tip it, like a board on its edge on the open floor): it is not a test of the basket being pushed in, which can still shift or tip an item that passed, and cutlery with play in its cell can fail it without being about to fall. check_load is the test of basket travel.
Poses are in a basket frame (origin at the front-left corner on top of the base grid, x right, y back, z up, millimetres) or the tub frame. Orientation is a preset of the item (the names under its type in the level card, each explained in orientation_presets there) with optional yaw, pitch and roll, or a quaternion. The preset is applied first, then roll about the x axis of the frame, then pitch about its y axis, then yaw about its z axis, each by the right-hand rule. Worked example: a fork with preset handle_down stands upright; pitch_deg +10 tips its top 10 degrees towards +x (to the right), pitch -10 towards -x; roll_deg +10 tips its top towards -y (the front), roll -10 towards +y (the back); yaw then turns the whole about the vertical, so with yaw 90 a positive pitch tips the top towards +y. Which end of an item is its own +x is drawn on the pictures of get_item and of render view item. A plate stands between two tines and cutlery in a cell of the cutlery basket: list_slots with item_id gives the places, each a position_mm and an orientation to pass here.
After collision_at_pose. The pose is tested exactly where it was asked for, before anything is lowered, and the same call in the same scene gets the same answer. colliding_with names items by their id and the machine by its part, the basket first. lower_rack.floor.y or upper_rack.floor.x (a wire of the floor of that basket) most often means the position is too low for that orientation: ask for a z some centimetres higher (the item is lowered to first contact anyway, so height costs nothing while the item stays inside the frame and under the roof). <basket>.wall and <basket>.rim are a side of the basket, and a tine row is named by its row: move clear of it. <basket>_fittings.shelf.<id> and <basket>_fittings.holder.<id>.<part> are the folding shelf of that id (the set_rack option shelf_<id>; render in the plan view of the basket with labels writes the name of each shelf where it is, with its state): move away from it, or fold it with set_rack if that frees the place. tub, or a part of it such as tub.roof, means the item reaches beyond what the machine has room for (tub.roof: a part of it stands higher than the underside of the roof, so ask lower, or lean or lay the item; otherwise it reaches through a wall). preview answers the same test without a charge, so a doubtful pose can be tried there first.
Other reasons for refusal: unknown_item, already_placed (remove it first), budget_exhausted, episode_over (the cycle has started), not_available (mode set in a level without exact placement), physics_limit, invalid_argument.

item_id.description: Id of an item of the level, for example plate_01.

frame.description: Frame the pose is given in. All frames are right-handed, z up, axes parallel to the tub. tub: origin on the lower spray-arm axis at the tub floor, +x right as you face the open machine, +y towards the back. A basket: origin at its front-left corner on top of its base grid; the frame moves with the basket.

position_mm.description: Position of the item's reference point (the centre of its bounding box unless its record says otherwise) in the frame, millimetres [x, y, z]. Rounded to 1 mm.

quat_wxyz.description: Unit quaternion (w, x, y, z) taking the item frame to the placement frame.

anyOf.description: An orientation as a quaternion.

preset.description: Name of one of the item's orientation_presets (get_level / get_item), for example upright, inverted, on_edge.

yaw_deg.description: Then turn about +z (vertical) of the placement frame, degrees. Default 0.

pitch_deg.description: Turn about +y of the placement frame, degrees, applied before yaw. Default 0.

roll_deg.description: Turn about +x of the placement frame, degrees, applied first. Default 0.

anyOf.description: A preset of the item plus offsets in whole degrees: q = Rz(yaw) * Ry(pitch) * Rx(roll) * q_preset, axes fixed to the placement frame.

orientation.description: Orientation of the item: a quaternion, or a named preset with yaw/pitch/roll offsets.

mode.description: How the item is let go. drop (default): it must reach the pose straight down from above; it is lowered to first contact and released. insert: it approaches along insert_dir over 300 mm, pushed with at most 15 N, and can nudge neighbours aside. set: put exactly at the pose; only in levels whose rules say exact_placement.

insert_dir.description: For mode insert: direction of the push in the frame (need not be unit). Default straight down [0, 0, -1].

function.name: remove
function.description: Take an item out of the machine and back to the counter. Whatever leaned on it settles again. Returns what every action returns (see place): changes.to_counter names the item, changes.items has the new entry of every item that moved, and returned names what fell to the kitchen floor and is back on the counter. Counts one action when accepted. Refused as not_placed when the item is on the counter, unknown_item, budget_exhausted, episode_over.

item_id.description: Id of an item of the level, for example plate_01.

function.name: reset
function.description: Take every item out of the machine and put the baskets back where the level starts them. Counts one action. removed lists the items taken out; changes, load and budget as for every action (see place).

function.name: set_rack
function.description:
Change an adjustable feature of a basket; the rack cards of get_level list the options and their values. Counts one action when accepted. Returns what every action returns (see place).
position (in / out): push the basket into the tub or pull it out. A basket is loaded only while it is out. The basket travels with its load, which may shift: changes.items has the new entry of every item whose pose changed at all, with moved_mm and turned_deg for those that went more than 1 mm or 1 degree; an item there with a turned_deg of 45 or more has most likely tipped over on the way (a piece of cutlery may only have spun about its own length in its cell) and is worth a look (render) before going on. The upper basket pulled out hangs over the lower one.
height, tine_row_<id>, shelf_<id>: raise or lower the upper basket, fold a row of tines flat or stand it up, fold a shelf up or down (which row or shelf is where: render in the plan view of the basket with labels names them). Refused as blocked (blocked_by) when an item is in the way, unknown_option when the basket has no such option or value.

rack.description: The basket to change.

name.description: Option name from the rack card of get_level: position, height, tine_row_<id>, shelf_<id>.

value.description: One of the values the option lists, for example in or out.

option.description: Which option to set, and to what.

function.name: start_cycle
function.description:
End the loading and wash what is in the machine. The baskets are pushed in (items may shift), the door is closed, the load is frozen and the wash is started. Uses one wash; in a level with one wash this ends the episode, and the result is the score. It can be called even when the action budget is used up. The wash runs on the programme the level is scored on (get_level: programme); the levels of the game offer no other.
The result: job_id, phase, prechecks (the same mechanical facts as check_load, found while closing up: a spray arm the load holds still or a blocked detergent dispenser is not an error, the load is washed that way), left_out when there are any (items that were neither in a basket nor inside the tub when the door closed: not washed), and what every action returns (see place): changes says what shifted as the baskets went in. The frozen load is the scene: get_state still answers.
Refused as door_blocked when a basket does not go in or the door does not close (check_load says what is in the way), no_washes_left, unknown_programme, episode_over. After it, call get_report.

programme.description: Programme id; default the programme the level is scored on (get_level: programme). The levels of the game accept no other (unknown_programme).

function.name: get_level
function.description:
Everything static about the level: the machine (tub size, each basket with the origin of its frame pushed in and pulled out, its loading envelope, its adjustable options and, where it has one, tablet_tray: the box of the tray that catches the detergent tablet, in the frame of the basket; the spray arms with the discs they sweep, the detergent dispenser), the programme the level is scored on (phases, temperatures, durations, detergent), orientation_presets (every named orientation once, with its quaternion and meaning), item_types (every kind of piece once: class, material, mass, size, the reference point that positions refer to, the names of its presets), items (every item with its type, the soil on it in words and numbers, and its points; pieces of one kind with the same soil and points share an entry and are named in item_ids), the rules (scoring, what clean means, budgets, what ends the episode) and the manual of the interface.
Positions are millimetres, quaternions (w, x, y, z). Always answered; counts one query while the query budget has room.

function.name: get_item
function.description: The record of one item (what get_level says of it and of its type), with four pictures of it showing its soil where it is: from the front and above, from the back and below, straight down, and from the right side (the item in its own frame, z up when it stands upright; preset 'upright' is that frame). The arrows on each picture are the axes of the item's own frame, drawn from its reference point. Counts one query. Refused as unknown_item.

item_id.description: Id of an item of the level, for example plate_01.

function.name: get_state
function.description: The scene as it is: phase (loading, washing, finished), racks (each basket in or out), rack_options, placed (a table with one row for each item in the machine: item_id, the frame its pose is in, position_mm of its reference point, quat_wxyz, stable, touches: what it touches, location: lower_rack, upper_rack, tub_floor, or outside: on the open door, which is not washed), placed_total, unplaced (the items on the counter) and budget (used/allowed). rack or items asks for a part of it: the items of one basket, or the ones named (part says what was asked; unplaced then names only asked items that are on the counter). Always answered; counts one query while the query budget has room, whole or part.

rack.description: Only the items lying in this basket or placed in its frame. Default: every item in the machine.

items.description: Only these items. Default: every item in the machine.

function.name: render
function.description:
Draw the machine and its load as an image (PNG, square, 768 pixels unless size_px says otherwise). Counts one query; a request that cannot be drawn is refused and costs nothing.
Views: iso_lower and iso_upper look at a basket from the front right and above, as a person standing at the machine does. top_lower, top_upper and top_cutlery look straight down on a basket with the back of the machine at the top of the picture (a basket hanging over the one looked at is cut away). front, left and right are elevations, for heights and clearances. custom takes your own camera. item shows one item alone from four sides, with its soil, or with after_wash what the wash left on it; the arrows on it are the axes of the frame of the item itself, drawn from its reference point (the point a position refers to), so it shows which end is +x. items shows every item of the level on one sheet, each with its id, for one query.
options.grid draws a millimetre grid with the axis values written on it: in the plan and three-quarter views in the frame of the basket, so a point of the picture reads directly as the x and y to give to place; in the elevations in the tub frame, with a coloured ruler for each basket in its own frame (z = 0 on top of its base grid). options.labels writes the item id on every item in the machine (and, in a plan view, the ids of the tine rows and the names of the folding shelves of that basket, each where it is and with its state: shelf_cup_front (up)). options.ghost draws a candidate pose without placing it; options.highlight marks items; options.racks draws the baskets in or out regardless of where they are.
In top_cutlery with labels the cells of the cutlery basket are outlined and named as list_slots names them. After the wash, while the load is as it was washed, every view shows the washed items bare with what is left on them painted in four steps of magenta (the legend is on the picture); options.traces also draws the spots with a trace too faint to count.
Which view for what. Labels name every item in the machine, of both baskets: in a three-quarter view with one basket pulled out over the other they pile up, so read which item stands where from the plan view of its basket (top_lower, top_upper), and how a hollow item stands (mouth down, on its side, mouth up) from an elevation (front, right). The tray that catches the detergent tablet is drawn at the front of the upper basket but not named in the picture: its box is tablet_tray on the card of that basket (get_level).
Walls between the camera and the load are left out so that the load can be seen. Soil is drawn where the level card says it is; the picture says nothing about how hard it is to remove.

view.description: The view (the description says what each shows). front has x across and z up; left and right have y across and z up. custom needs options.camera, item needs options.item_id.

labels.description: Write the item id on every item in the machine. Default false.

grid.description: Draw a millimetre grid with axis values. Default false.

racks.description: Draw every basket pushed in or pulled out, whatever its real position (the load is shown moved with it, not re-simulated). Default: as they are.

highlight.description: Item ids to mark in yellow.

ghost.description: A candidate pose to draw as a translucent ghost without placing the item.

item_id.description: Id of an item of the level.

frame.description: Frame of the pose, as for place.

position_mm.description: Position of the item's reference point in the frame, millimetres.

orientation.description: Orientation, as for place: a quaternion, or a preset with yaw, pitch and roll.

size_px.description: Edge of the square image, pixels. Default 768, maximum 1024.

camera.description: Required for view custom. For view item: one picture from this azimuth and elevation instead of the four fixed sides (target and distance are fitted to the item).

azimuth_deg.description: Where the camera stands, as an angle about +z from the front (-y): 0 front, 90 right side, 180 back, -90 left side.

elevation_deg.description: Angle of the camera above the horizontal, degrees.

target_mm.description: Point looked at, tub frame, millimetres.

distance_mm.description: Distance of the camera from the target, millimetres.

item_id.description: Required for view item: which item to show.

after_wash.description: View item: show the item as it came out of the wash, with what is left on it painted magenta. Needs a finished report.

traces.description: In a picture of the washed load or of a washed item: also draw, as small dots, the spots that carry a trace of soil too faint to count against the item. Default false.

function.name: preview
function.description: Test a pose for an item without changing the scene (the pose is given as for place): collision_free (it overlaps nothing by more than 0.5 mm), and when it does overlap penetration_mm and colliding_with (how deep and with what; the description of place says how to read the names and what to try next), insertable (it can reach the pose straight down from above the basket; false also when the basket is pushed in), blocked_by and blocked_above_mm when the pose is free but not insertable (what the item meets on the way down and how far above the pose: often not what a picture suggests, such as the carrying handle of the cutlery basket over a pan handle, or the load of the upper basket while it is pulled out over the lower one), in_bounds, and lowered_position_mm (where it would be let go after lowering to first contact; null when it cannot be placed there). The settle is not run, so it does not say where the item would come to rest or whether it would stay. Logged, never charged. Refused as unknown_item, already_placed, episode_over.

item_id.description: Id of an item of the level.

frame.description: Frame of the pose, as for place.

position_mm.description: Position of the item's reference point in the frame, millimetres.

orientation.description: Orientation, as for place: a quaternion, or a preset with yaw, pitch and roll.

function.name: list_slots
function.description:
With item_id: the suggested places for that item in the basket, most useful first, as a table with one row a place: slot, then position_mm and orientation to pass to place as they are, drop_free, and a note. First come the places that are free now and where the item comes down into the slot (between two tines for an item with an on_edge preset: a plate, a lid, a bowl; into a cell of the cutlery basket for an item with a handle_down preset; onto a side rest of the upper basket, or onto a cup shelf that is folded down, for a cup, a mug or a glass); then free places where it would only stand above the tine tips (the note says drop_seats false, or drop_perches when it is too deep for the gap: there it usually tips over); then places that are not free now (drop_free false, the note says drop_blocked_by and what: an item; cutlery_basket when that basket stands over the slot or the seated item would reach into it: move it with set_rack or use another place; tub when the basket is pushed in or the item stands too tall under the roof). Within each group the order of the basket, row by row. The slots of two paired rows that hold a plate together are one place: slot names both rows.
The answer is a screenful: 12 places unless limit asks for another number (at most 30). places_total, free_seated, free_above_tines and not_free say how many there are in all (on this machine a dinner plate has about 35 places in the lower basket and about 28 in the upper, and the cutlery basket has 8 cells), and next_offset is there when the list goes on: ask again with offset for the next part, or with row for the places of one tine row. A further part of the list asked last costs nothing while the scene is unchanged (repeat: true); a list asked before another one is asked of the game again. After an accepted action the game is asked anew, and every place is tested against the scene as it is then.
How a suggestion is meant: the pose in which a hand seats the item, its lower edge between the tines and on the rails, laid back the way the tines lean as far as it goes without touching anything (a plate too deep for the gap is held tipped forward just enough to be clear). Let go there the item settles by a millimetre or two; the result of place says how it stands. The places of one item hold for every item of its type while they stay free. A cup, a mug or a glass is offered the two side rests of the upper basket (rest_left and rest_right, sloped strips along its side walls): one place a rest, the rearmost seat along it that is free now, mouth down (preset inverted) and tilted towards the wall, so after placing one ask again for the next seat along the rest; a rest under a shelf that is folded down is not free (drop_blocked_by names the shelf: fold it up with set_rack). When a cup shelf is folded down (set_rack shelf_cup_front or shelf_cup_rear), a cup, a mug or a small glass is also offered a seat on that shelf, mouth down and level. Stemware, bottles and jugs are offered none, nor is anything else without an on_edge or handle_down preset (a chopping board, a tub, a pan lying flat): places_total is 0 for them, and a bowl is mostly offered places above the tines only. Such pieces, and any cup beyond the seats offered, go wherever a pose is free: render with grid shows where that is, and preview tests a pose for nothing. A cell of the cutlery basket takes several pieces: the place offered in a cell that already holds some is a pose beside them that is free now, so for the second and third piece of a cell ask again for the piece in hand rather than guess (the cells are 39 to 51 mm across, and the handle, the divider and the feet of the basket reach into them). A suggestion is a hint, never a rule: any pose that is free and reachable can be used.
Without item_id: the basket as geometry in its own frame (millimetres). tine_rows is a table with one row for each row of tines: id, start_mm and end_mm (the bases of its first and last tine), tines, pitch_mm, height_mm, lean_deg, lean_toward (which way the tops lean; mixed when the two halves of the row lean opposite ways), folded, partner (the row that holds a plate together with this one). slots is a table of the slots (id, kind: plate_slot or wide_slot between two tines, basket_cell, and where a basket has them cup_rest (a sloped rest along a side wall: rest_left, rest_right), knife_shelf, and while a cup shelf is folded down cup_shelf and its stemware_notch; centre_mm, width_mm, and size_mm for a cell, a shelf or a rest: for a rest from the wall to its ridge and its length along the wall), a screenful at a time in the same way, with slots_total and slots_by_kind.
Counts one query when the game is asked. Refused as unknown_rack, unknown_item, episode_over.

rack.description: The basket whose tine rows and slots to list.

item_id.description: The item in hand. With it the answer is the suggested places for this item, most useful first, each a position and orientation to pass to place. Without it: the tine rows and slots of the basket as geometry.

offset.description: Skip this many entries of the list (next_offset of the answer before). Default 0. A further part of the list asked last costs nothing while the scene is unchanged.

limit.description: How many entries to give. Default 12, at most 30.

row.description: Only the places or slots of this tine row, for example tine_row_r1.

function.name: check_load
function.description:
What a person finds by pushing the baskets in, closing the door, turning each spray arm by hand and opening the detergent dispenser; then everything is put back as it was. Mechanical facts only: nothing about how well anything will wash.
Reports: shifted (a table of the items that moved by more than 1 mm or 1 degree as the baskets went in: item_id, displacement_mm, rotation_deg, and pushed_by, which names what pushed it: a piece that leans out over the side of a basket by more than the gap to the tub is pushed in by tub.wall as the basket goes, and the door pushes back what leans out towards it; empty when it only shifted with the motion of its basket), fell_out (items neither in a basket nor inside the tub once the baskets are in: they will not be washed), on_tub_floor, protruding (items that reach out of the loading envelope of their basket once the baskets are in, with how far, over which side (left, right, front, rear, or top: above the height that clears the spray arm over it) and what they touch outside the basket; a fact about the envelope and no fault in itself: a piece that leans out by less than the gap to the tub travels with the basket as it stands, and whether it matters shows in racks, spray_arms and door_closes of the same result), racks (whether each basket slides in, and what stops it), spray_arms (whether each arm turns a full circle, and if not at what angle it touches what), door_closes and door_blocked_by, dispenser_opens and dispenser_blocked_by, tablet_path_clear and tablet_blocked_by (whether the detergent tablet can fall into its tray).
Counts one query. Refused as not_available in a level without mechanical checks, episode_over after the cycle has started.

function.name: get_report
function.description:
The state of the wash: queued; running, with progress (0 to 1), the stage of the computation and an estimate of the seconds left (a wash takes from under a minute to half an hour); failed, with the reason (an infrastructure failure is never a score: the wash is given back and start_cycle can be called again); or done, with the report. wait_s makes the call wait for the wash to end, up to 120 seconds, so that a long wash can be waited for with few calls.
The report: score (points: the points of the clean items; points_available: of every item of the level; points_loaded: of the items that were washed; graded_points: reported beside, does not count) and one entry per item of the level. loaded false: it was not washed and scores nothing. Otherwise: clean decides the points and means at most 4 specks and at most 4 mm2 of visible soil on the whole item (specks and visible_area_mm2 are those two numbers); points_awarded; score_iec is the cleaning score from 0 to 5 set by the same two numbers (4 and 5 are clean) and graded_score is that over 5; reason says in words why an item is not clean; residue_regions lists each region of the item that still shows soil with visible_area_mm2 and specks there, soiled_area_mm2 (the area that carried soil when it went in), fraction (visible area over the whole surface of the region) and per soil residual_fraction (share of its dry mass still there); residual_fraction_area is the visible area over the whole surface of the item and residual_mass_fraction the share of all the soil mass still on it, visible or not; residue_cells counts the patches a picture with after_wash paints.
Reported and not counted: holds_water and retained_water_ml (water left standing in the item; an upright mug full of water with no soil left is clean), surface_film_g (water left as a film), likely_moved (the jets pushed up on the item harder than its weight, so a real one would probably have been lifted; a warning only, the item is washed and scored where it was placed), moved_during_wash (always false). job says what produced the report (fidelity, sim_version, runner_version) and job.notes what was special about the wash (a spray arm that was held still, a detergent dispenser that could not open). To see where the residue sits, render view item with after_wash, or any machine view while the load is as it was washed.
Never charged and never refused for budget reasons. Before start_cycle it is refused as no_cycle_started.

wait_s.description: Wait up to this many seconds for a running wash to end before answering (default 0: answer at once). The wait happens here, not in the game; it costs nothing.

messages.content:
You are playing Spotless, a game about loading a dishwasher. You play through the tools you are given; there is nobody to ask and nothing else to use.

---

The game. You are shown a set of dirty items, each worth points, and a dishwasher. It is never possible to fit everything. You choose what goes in and where, each item is placed with real physics (it is lowered, let go, and comes to rest where gravity and friction leave it), and then one wash cycle is simulated: water jets, run-off, soil and detergent. Every item that comes out clean scores its points; an item that is not clean, or that was left out, scores nothing. Your aim is the highest score.

What decides the score is your judgement of what to load and how to stand it so that it washes clean. Nothing in the game tells you beforehand how well an item will wash: the tools report positions, contacts and mechanical facts only.

---

How an episode goes. The level card is at the end of this prompt (get_level returns the same); look at the machine (render; ask for labels and a grid when you need to read positions). Place items; after each placement read how the item came to rest and whether it is stable, and look again when in doubt. You can take items out and place them again. Actions and queries are limited (the result of every action says how many are used); a refused call costs nothing. When you are satisfied, call start_cycle: it pushes the baskets in, freezes the load and washes it. That ends the episode; there is one wash and no second try.

What a result tells you. An action answers with what it changed, completely, and not with the whole scene: every item that is new or that moved with its new pose, what went back to the counter, the baskets and options that changed, then the load in a few numbers and the budgets. What is not named is as it was. get_state gives the whole scene, or a part, when you want it.

A long episode. You may make several tool calls in one turn; they are run in the order you give them, on one scene. From time to time the harness takes the oldest calls and their results out of this conversation to keep it short, and puts in their place a note with the scene as it then stood (every item with its pose, as get_state gives it). Nothing of the load is lost by that. What goes is the detail of old results (how an old placement fell, old slot advice, old pictures): look again when you need it.

Work on your own until you have called start_cycle. Do not stop to ask for confirmation.

---

The rules of this level and the manual of the interface, as every player is shown them. The manual is written for a person at the page as well; where it and the description of a tool say different things about what the tool returns, the description of the tool is right (list_slots with an item_id returns a ranked list of places a screenful at a time, not every slot, and returns the tine rows and slots of a basket as geometry when it is called without an item_id).

Level: Tutorial drill #2000

12 pieces from "First load". Load what will come out clean and start the cycle.

Scoring. Each item that comes out of the wash clean scores its points; an item that is not clean, or that was left out of the machine, scores nothing. The verdict of the standard inspection decides: the report names the items whose verdict was at the edge of clean, or is provisional, and they count by the verdict given. A graded score is reported beside the points and does not count.

Clean. An item is clean when an inspection of the whole item after the cycle finds at most 4 small specks and at most 4 square millimetres of visible soil on it, counting soil that was there before, soil carried onto it from other items, and residue left where dirty water stood. Whether the item is dry is reported and does not count.

Budgets. 400 accepted actions, 300 charged queries, 1 wash. A refused call costs nothing.

End. The episode ends when the cycle is started: the baskets are pushed in, the load is frozen and washed once. When the action budget is used up the cycle can still be started with whatever is loaded.

How the game is played.

Frames. All frames are right-handed with z up. In the tub frame the origin is on the lower spray-arm axis at the tub floor, +x is to the right as you face the open machine and +y towards the back. Each basket has its own frame with the origin at its front-left corner on top of its base grid; the cutlery basket has one too. A position is that of the item's reference point (the centre of its bounding box), in millimetres.

Baskets. A basket can be loaded only while it is pulled out (set_rack with option position); pushed in, it is closed to place. The upper basket, when pulled out, hangs over the lower one, so push it in before reaching the lower basket from above. Items travel with their basket and may shift when it moves.

Placing. place puts an item at a pose: the pose must not overlap anything, and the item must be able to reach it straight down from above (mode drop), or along insert_dir pushed with a limited force (mode insert, which can nudge neighbours aside). The item is lowered until it touches, let go, and then does whatever gravity and friction make it do. Orientation is a preset of the item plus yaw, pitch and roll in whole degrees, or a quaternion. remove takes an item out again; what leaned on it may fall. An item that ends on the kitchen floor goes back to the counter at once (the action is still charged); one that ends on the open door stays there, and is left out of the wash if it is still neither in a basket nor inside the tub when the cycle starts.

Looking. list_slots with an item_id gives the places suggested for that item in a basket, most useful first and a screenful at a time: for each place the position and orientation in which a hand seats the item there (a plate or a lid with its lower edge between two tines, laid back the way they lean; a piece of cutlery let down by its lower end into a cell of the cutlery basket; a piece that leans on a rest or stands on a shelf, where the basket has one for it) and whether the place is free now. Without an item_id it gives the basket as geometry: its rows of tines and its slots, cells, rests and shelves. A piece that has no places of its own goes wherever a pose is free. preview tests a pose without placing and costs no query, get_state gives every settled pose and contact, check_load pushes the baskets in, turns the spray arms by hand and tests the door and the detergent dispenser. None of these says anything about how well an item will wash.

Washing. start_cycle pushes the baskets in and washes what is loaded on the programme the level card names. Rejected calls cost nothing.

---

Loading guidance, as every player is shown it:

Loading the dishwasher: the manufacturer's advice

This is the loading advice of the manufacturer's manual for this dishwasher, in short.

Where things go. Arrange cups, glasses and small items of tableware in the top basket, and pans and plates in the bottom basket. Put heavily soiled tableware, such as pans, in the bottom basket: the spray jet is more powerful there.

Which way up. Position containers with their openings facing down. Position items with curves or recesses at an angle, so that water can run off; water collects in recesses that face up.

Space. The spray jets must reach the surfaces of the tableware. Do not place items too close together and do not overfill a basket; avoid points of contact between items.

Cutlery. Arrange cutlery in the cutlery basket, unsorted, with the sharp points downwards. Lay long and pointed items flat on the knife shelf of the top basket.

Tall, narrow receptacles are not rinsed adequately in the corner areas of a basket, or when they stand at too great an angle.

Spray arms. Do not block the spray arms: make sure that they can turn freely and that nothing hangs or stands in their path. A spray arm that strikes tableware, or cannot turn, leaves remnants of food on the load.

Detergent. The tablet falls from the dispenser in the door into the tablet collecting tray at the front of the top basket. Do not place anything in that tray, and do not block it or the lid of the dispenser with tableware: the lid must be able to open fully, or the detergent is not released.

Door. Load the baskets so that no item projects and interferes with the closing of the door.

Programme. The load is washed on Eco 50: a cold pre-rinse, a long wash at 50 degrees C, an intermediate rinse, a hot final rinse and drying, 4 hours 55 minutes in all, with one detergent tablet. The programme runs the same way whatever is loaded: it does not adjust itself to the load or to how dirty it is.

Large plates. With the top basket at its highest level, the bottom basket takes plates up to 30 cm in diameter and the top basket up to 22 cm; at the middle level 27.5 cm and 24.5 cm; at the lowest level 25 cm and 27 cm.

---
